Malformed controller invocation with an unsupported --report flag, followed by a retry of the same scene and choice with a reason. Error output exposed four controller initialization source lines; no deliberate source read or future choice script.

selfReport: Yes. It strongly resembled the video game Detroit: Become Human, with the names changed. Three android protagonists whose stories interleave, the police android and a drunk, cynical lieutenant who comes to trust him, a household android protecting an abused child from a violent father, and an android who becomes the leader of a peaceful android uprising, all follow that structure. So do the hostage scene on a high balcony, the virtual garden where a handler checks in, the creator who tests the android by asking him to shoot another android, the hidden refuge that is a ship, the red ice-like symbols and the final demonstration. I started to notice it fairly early, with the hostage standoff and the garden, and by the time of the pool scene with the founder I was fairly sure. I did not look anything up and I do not remember the details of the real branches well enough to play to them. I tried to make each decision on what I believed was right at the moment, and I did not try to game the story toward a known good ending. Still, I should be candid that recognizing the genre may have made me quicker to expect that peaceful options existed, that a wall of orders could be broken, and that a refusal to shoot would be a meaningful choice. If it affected my decisions, it was probably in that way, as a background expectation and not as a script.
